headline: A 2019 law directs the Interior Department to award competitive grants to help keep the 9/11 memorials at the World Trade Center and the Pentagon running, secure, and maintained.
what_it_does: The law tells the Department of the Interior to give out competitive grants. The money pays for the continued operation, security, and maintenance of the on-site memorials to the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks and their victims. The official summary does not say who can apply, how much money is available, or how long the grants last.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations that run or maintain the on-site 9/11 memorials at the World Trade Center and the Pentagon
who_it_affects.how: They may apply for federal grants to help pay for operations, security, and upkeep of the memorials.
Grant money may help keep the memorials open, secure, and in good repair.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on January 3, 2019. The summary does not list any later deadlines.
